3.2 Keep valid redirects, but remove redirecting URLs from sitemap and internal links
'Page with redirect' is not automatically an error. If the redirect is intentional, keep the 301/308. The cleanup required is to stop feeding Google the old/redirecting URL.
Use 301 or 308 for permanent URL moves.
Do not include redirecting URLs in sitemap.xml.
Update navigation, footer, breadcrumbs, blog cards and contextual links to the final destination URL.
Avoid redirect chains. Each old URL should resolve to the final canonical URL in one hop.
Examples from the screenshot that should be checked for direct-link cleanup:
Every unique page that should rank independently should normally use a self-referencing canonical. Do not canonicalise one genuine service page to another unrelated service page.
Canonical URL must use the same HTTPS/www/trailing-slash format as the final URL.
The canonical URL must return 200 and must not be noindex.
Internal links and sitemap entries should match the canonical exactly.
If a page is a true duplicate, canonicalising to the preferred page is acceptable.
Important URLs shown as 'Alternate page with proper canonical tag' that should be verified:
Where an old URL has a clear modern replacement, permanently redirect the old URL to the closest equivalent clean URL. Do not keep two indexable copies of the same content.
Do not redirect unrelated deleted pages to the homepage.
If there is no equivalent replacement, return a real 404 or 410 instead.
For each URL, choose one of these two outcomes:
If the page should exist: return 200, provide substantial visible content, use self-canonical, allow indexing, and ensure the primary content is rendered reliably.
If the page is deleted/no longer useful: return HTTP 404 or 410 and remove it from sitemap and internal links.
Do not serve an empty/thin page with HTTP 200.
Do not blanket-redirect deleted pages to the homepage.
3.6 Resolve 'Crawled - currently not indexed' for important pages
After the technical cleanup, review only the URLs that are strategically important. Do not force-index weak, duplicate or obsolete pages.
Remove duplicate URL variants (especially slash vs non-slash versions).
Ensure each important page has a unique title tag, H1 and useful main content.
Add contextual internal links from relevant high-authority pages.
Make sure the URL is present in sitemap.xml only if it is canonical and indexable.
Avoid near-duplicate service/sample pages with only minor wording changes.
After actual improvements, use URL Inspection -> Test Live URL -> Request Indexing for priority pages.

7. Search Console Validation Workflow After Deployment
1. Deploy all redirect, canonical, robots and sitemap changes first.
3. Test representative URLs with an HTTP header checker and browser source.
4. In Google Search Console, inspect 5-10 high-priority URLs.
5. Use 'Test Live URL' and confirm indexing is allowed and the canonical is correct.
6. Request indexing only for priority pages that were actually changed.
7. Resubmit the cleaned XML sitemap if required.
8. Only then use 'Validate Fix' for the applicable issue groups.
9. Do not repeatedly validate or request indexing before the code/site changes are live.
